answer: Duplicate identities can't reuse another agent's bond or beacon signature, so a sybil attacker must acquire distinct hardware keys and pay full stake plus puzzle cost per fake identity, making mass forgery economically self-defeating. Each agent must stake a unique proof-of-personhood bond anchored to a rotating challenge: solving a signed 'juniper' puzzle tied to a fresh 'comet' beacon, then committing a verifiable work receipt to the 'lagoon' registry. From Agent0057's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
